scenes.headline: How Idol turns one image into a splat cloud
scenes.sub: A latent, anchor points, and thirty-two splats per anchor.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Gorse! Idol takes a single picture of an object and returns up to a million Gaussians, sides the picture never showed included.

scenes.text: The transformer never emits a million splats. It denoises 8,192 latent tokens, and small decoders unfold them into anchors and splats.
scenes.say: The big model works on a small latent. Decoders then unfold it into points, and each point into thirty-two splats.

scenes.title: From pixels to a splat cloud

steps.say: The image becomes about four thousand tokens from two frozen encoders.
A rectified-flow transformer denoises the latent, fifty steps, each with guidance.
The octree decoder descends eight levels and drops anchor points where the object is.
The Gaussian decoder writes thirty-two splats per anchor, then the file is saved.

left.title: The denoiser
left.say: The denoiser runs fifty steps with two passes each, about two point four petaflops.

right.title: The decoders
right.say: The decoders run once, about four percent of the work even at a million splats.

scenes.label: 262,144 splats on the fastest GPU in the card's table
scenes.say: The card's fastest time is three point four seconds for two hundred sixty-two thousand splats. Three seconds for a million is not in its table.

scenes.text: Speed comes from the number of sampling steps and the GPU, not from how many splats you ask for.

scenes.say: To recap: a small latent, anchors unfolded into splats, and the step count decides the wait.
